name: Axel Lehmann

summary.text: Axel P. Lehmann was appointed chairman of Credit Suisse Group on January 17, 2022, after António Horta-Osório resigned, and chaired the bank through its collapse. In December 2022 he said in interviews that client outflows had basically stopped; FINMA investigated those statements and announced on March 10, 2023 that it found no sufficient grounds to open proceedings, while setting out expectations for the bank's future communications. On March 19, 2023 the Swiss Federal Council adopted emergency measures enabling UBS to acquire Credit Suisse for CHF 3 billion, and FINMA ordered Credit Suisse's AT1 instruments of around CHF 16 billion written off. Lehmann was narrowly re-elected and apologised to shareholders at the bank's final annual meeting in April 2023.

facts.claim: Credit Suisse's board appointed Axel P. Lehmann as chairman, effective immediately, on January 17, 2022, after António Horta-Osório resigned after about nine months in the role.
facts.quote: Credit Suisse Group appoints Axel P. Lehmann as new Chairman; António Horta-Osório has resigned

sources.title: Credit Suisse Group appoints Axel P. Lehmann as new Chairman; António Horta-Osório has resigned

facts.claim: In February 2023 Bloomberg and swissinfo reported that FINMA was reviewing whether Lehmann's December 2022 comments that outflows had 'basically stopped' were misleading, and that Credit Suisse's 2022 results showed fourth-quarter outflows of about CHF 111 billion, roughly CHF 25 billion more than at the time of his statements.
facts.quote: Lehmann had described the outflows as "basically stopped" in a Bloomberg interview.

sources.title: Credit Suisse Chairman's Outflow Claims Probed, Reuters Says
Watchdog calls off investigation into Credit Suisse chairman

facts.claim: On March 10, 2023 FINMA announced that after completing its investigations into statements about outflows of client funds at Credit Suisse it found no sufficient grounds to open supervisory proceedings, and set out what it expected of the bank regarding future communications.
facts.quote: FINMA sees no sufficient grounds for proceedings following investigations into statements on outflows of client funds at Credit Suisse

sources.title: FINMA sees no sufficient grounds for proceedings following investigations into statements on outflows of client funds at Credit Suisse
Watchdog calls off investigation into Credit Suisse chairman

facts.claim: On March 19, 2023 FINMA approved the merger of UBS and Credit Suisse and ordered Credit Suisse to write off its AT1 instruments of around CHF 16 billion, determining that a contractual 'viability event' had occurred once the government guarantee was put in place; UBS paid CHF 3 billion, equal to CHF 0.76 per Credit Suisse share.
facts.quote: FINMA's own release puts it at around CHF 16 billion, and thus an increase in core capital.

sources.title: FINMA approves merger of UBS and Credit Suisse
UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse, 19 March 2023 (investor presentation)

facts.claim: The Swiss Federal Council adopted an emergency package on March 19, 2023 enabling the takeover, including SNB liquidity backed by a federal guarantee, federal guarantees for potential losses on certain assets UBS acquired, and a clearer legal basis for FINMA to write off part of Credit Suisse's regulatory capital.
facts.quote: FINMA was provided with a clearer legal basis so that part of Credit Suisse's regulatory capital could be written off.

sources.title: UBS takeover of Credit Suisse

facts.claim: At Credit Suisse's final shareholder meeting on April 4, 2023 Lehmann apologised to shareholders and was narrowly re-elected as chairman.
facts.quote: Credit Suisse chair re-elected after apology at final shareholder meeting

sources.title: Credit Suisse chair re-elected after apology at final shareholder meeting

facts.claim: FINMA's December 19, 2023 report 'Lessons Learned from the CS Crisis' found that Credit Suisse lost the confidence of its clients, investors and the markets and that the resulting withdrawals of client funds created a risk of immediate insolvency in mid-March 2023; it states FINMA had asked the bank from summer 2022 to prepare for an emergency and confirms it investigated the outflow statements and concluded they were not grounds for proceedings.
facts.quote: from summer 2022 onwards, FINMA also asked the bank to take various measures to prepare for an emergency

sources.title: FINMA Report: Lessons Learned from the CS Crisis
FINMA publishes report and lessons learned from the Credit Suisse crisis

facts.claim: In October 2025 the Swiss Federal Administrative Court issued a partial decision in the case brought by former AT1 holders, finding that FINMA's write-off order lacked a sufficient legal basis and revoking the decree, with remedies to be considered later; FINMA said it would appeal to the Federal Supreme Court.
facts.quote: The court determined that FINMA's order lacked a sufficient legal basis and revoked FINMA's decree.

sources.title: Court ruling related to write-off of Credit Suisse AT1 capital

openQuestions: Site claim that FINMA wrote CHF 16 billion of AT1 bonds down to zero while shareholders received about CHF 3 billion in UBS shares: supported by FINMA's March 19, 2023 release and UBS's presentation (CHF 3 billion, CHF 0.76 per share); FINMA's later report gives CHF 16.5 billion nominal and UBS CHF 15.8 billion.

Site claim that the Federal Council used emergency powers under Articles 184 and 185 of the Federal Constitution to bypass shareholder votes: the Federal Department of Finance confirms emergency measures enabling the takeover; the specific constitutional articles and the shareholder-vote point were not confirmed by the sources returned.
Site claim of 'roughly 32 billion Swiss francs in bonuses' over the decade (Tages-Anzeiger calculation): not researched.

Site claim that UBS received a CHF 9 billion federal loss-protection agreement and CHF 100 billion liquidity backstop: the Federal Department of Finance page describes loss guarantees and SNB liquidity with a federal guarantee, but the specific amounts were not confirmed by the sources returned.
The October 2025 Federal Administrative Court decision revoking FINMA's AT1 decree is under appeal per UBS's summary; the Federal Supreme Court outcome was not found.
